text:
jess: Heads-up: after yesterday's kernel-router tweak I'm seeing ~2x p99 on a few Mistral-heavy routes. Quick gut says KV-cache churn + kernel fallback == latency spike.

runtime-bot: [perf-alert] route=gen-mistral-highseq p95=210ms p99=820ms (baseline p99 ~380ms) :rotating_light:

tomas: Can you paste a short flame or the runtime trace? curious if it's prefetch or eviction churn.

jess: Pasted a trimmed trace below (stack from runtime profiler). Note repeated evict/prefetch loops around same keys.
```
[profiler] t=0.003s select_kernel(mistral_v1, seq=1024) -> fallback(fp16_kernel)
[kvcache] lookup hit=0 miss=1 fetch_prefetch kp=0.79ms
[kvcache] insert size=64KB -> evict candidate=head-idx=12 age=1
[kernel] run fp16_kernel size=8192 -> 12ms
[kvcache] evict head-idx=12 freed=64KB
[kvcache] lookup hit=0 miss=1 fetch_prefetch kp=0.81ms
... repeated ~8x ...
```

sara: That's very suggestive of "entry size inflation" when RoPE scaling + head_dim mismatch makes quantized KV entries larger than expected. We recently changed RoPE scaling table for Mistral in the tokenizer branch.

mira: Hypothesis: RoPE change changed effective seq->kv layout (padding/alignment), which interacts poorly with our FP8 quantized layout and causes entries to cross slab boundaries. Eviction then thrashes small-LRU buckets.

sam: Two quick levers: (1) kernel-selector threshold: prefer same-precision kernels when seq-length above 512 even if estimated throughput lower (avoid fallback cost). (2) KV-layout change: switch to interleaved 8-bit packing that keeps per-head data contiguous to avoid crossing slab pages. Both cheap to toggle.

tomas: Agree. Also try switching eviction policy from pure LRU to frequency-weighted-LRU (LFU-ish) for these routes; repeated cold misses for the same prefixes are killing us.

jess: Trying an experiment patch now. Plan:
- runtime flag: prefer_same_precision_for_long_seq=true
- kvcfg: pack_mode=interleaved8
- eviction: policy=weighted_lru, weight_decay=0.6
- add extra profiling: kv.stats(detailed=true) and kernel-router.trace=on

sara: When you run, capture these counters: kv.max_entry_bytes, kv.avg_entries_per_key, kernel.fallback_count, kernel.switch_latency_ms. Those will prove the loop.

jess: Running on canary now (dedicated pool small test). Attaching short log snippet after 5m: 
```
CANARY LOG [5m]
route=gen-mistral-highseq: p99->430ms (was 820ms)
kernel.fallback_count=2 (was 18)
kv.max_entry_bytes=65536 (was 131072)
kv.evictions_per_min=2.1 (was 9.4)
```

mira: Nice — fallback_count down is promising. kv.max_entry_bytes halved suggests packing helped. Any regression in quality?

jess: No visible quality change on the smoke prompts. We still need to validate longer prompts and multi-turn.

sam: If this holds, we should: (A) land interleaved8 as route-opt-in for Mistral variants, (B) relax kernel-router optimizer to add a seq-length override, (C) add a conservative heuristic: if eviction rate > 5/min then temporarily bias away from FP8 cache.

tomas: Also add a quickness: instrument head-dim alignment check at model onboarding. If head_dim % 16 != 0 or rope_scale != expected, flag a "kv-layout-risk" tag so runtime can choose safer packing by default.

jess: I'll open a small PR with: config flags, canary rollout plan, and the profiling dashboard links. Will ping infra to extend retention for kv.stats for 48h.

sara: Thanks. Can we also add a tiny integration test that simulates misaligned heads (pad+seq) so future RoPE/tokenizer changes fail fast?

jess: Good call — adding test to runtime-unit (small synthetic workload that hits eviction loop).

mira: TL;DR: root cause likely RoPE->layout interaction + FP8 packing crossing slab boundaries -> eviction thrash -> kernel fallback amplifies latency. Fix path: pack change + selector heuristics + eviction guard.

sam: I'll draft the kernel-router knobs doc with recommended thresholds.

runtime-bot: deploy (canary) started by jess on pool=dedicated-canary-3 at 1867543270

jess: Will report back with 24h data. Thanks all :pray:
